steps.title: Initialize a Git Repository
steps.description: Create a new project directory and initialize Git version control.
tasks: Create a directory called `myproject`: `mkdir ~/myproject && cd ~/myproject`
Initialize Git: `git init`
Verify: `ls -la .git` to confirm the .git directory exists

steps.title: Make Your First Commits
steps.description: Create files, stage them, and commit snapshots of your project.
tasks: Create a file: `echo '# My Project' > README.md`
Stage it: `git add README.md`
Commit: `git commit -m "Initial commit: add README"`
Add another file: `echo 'console.log("hello")' > app.js && git add app.js && git commit -m "Add app.js"`

verification.command: cd /home/student/myproject && git log --oneline | wc -l | awk '{if ($1 >= 2) print "PASS"; else print "FAIL"}'

steps.title: Create and Merge a Feature Branch
steps.description: Practice the feature branch workflow used by all professional development teams.
tasks: Create and switch to a new branch: `git checkout -b feature/add-styles`
Create a CSS file: `echo 'body { color: cyan; }' > style.css`
Stage and commit: `git add style.css && git commit -m "Add styling"`
Switch back to main and merge: `git checkout main && git merge feature/add-styles`

verification.command: cd /home/student/myproject && git log --oneline | grep -i 'style\|styling' && test -f style.css && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: Simulate and Resolve a Merge Conflict
steps.description: Create a deliberate conflict between two branches and resolve it manually.
tasks: On main: `echo 'version = 1.0' > config.txt && git add config.txt && git commit -m "Add config v1"`
Create branch: `git checkout -b hotfix && echo 'version = 1.1-hotfix' > config.txt && git add . && git commit -m "Hotfix version"`
Go back to main: `git checkout main && echo 'version = 2.0' > config.txt && git add . && git commit -m "Version 2"`
Merge: `git merge hotfix` — resolve the conflict in config.txt, then `git add config.txt && git commit`

verification.command: cd /home/student/myproject && git log --oneline | head -1 | grep -v 'CONFLICT' && test -f config.txt && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: Use Git Stash
steps.description: Practice saving work-in-progress with git stash.
tasks: Make some changes: `echo 'work in progress...' >> app.js`
Stash them: `git stash save "WIP: app changes"`
Verify working directory is clean: `git status`
Restore the stash: `git stash pop`
Verify changes are back: `cat app.js`

verification.command: cd /home/student/myproject && grep -q 'work in progress' app.js && echo PASS || echo FAIL

steps.title: Tag a Release
steps.description: Create a version tag to mark a release milestone.
tasks: Commit any remaining changes: `git add . && git commit -m "Prepare for release" 2>/dev/null || true`
Create an annotated tag: `git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "First stable release"`
Verify the tag: `git tag` and `git show v1.0.0`

verification.command: cd /home/student/myproject && git tag | grep -q 'v1.0.0' && echo PASS || echo FAIL
